list: The official 55 trophies as PlayStation publishes them, listed via Exophase and PSNProfiles, which agree on every name, description and grade. Every guide below was written for this entry and cites its sources.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own once the other 54 trophies are earned, so treat it as the finish line of the roadmap rather than a target of its own. Work the stages in order — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles, then money and robberies — and keep an eye on the missable flags before you play the final mission. The last trophy standing is usually A Long Road (100% completion); when that lands, this one follows.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It unlocks automatically as you play the prologue — there is nothing to hunt down and no way to miss it, because the game opens with this mission. If you are replaying for a clean file, this is the first trophy you will see.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and this unlocks at the chapter's end. Story chapters cannot be skipped or locked out, so just follow the main markers. Use the chapter to learn the map's first regions and start the activity trophies early if you like — nothing in Chapter 1 closes anything off.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Awarded for completing Chapter 2, in the same automatic way as the other chapter trophies. Play the story missions in order; the trophy lands when the chapter wraps. Before you push deep into Chapter 2, glance at the stranger strands (Stage 2 of the roadmap) — starting them early keeps the missable character trophies safe.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 to earn this. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable — the story carries you through it. By this point most of Leonida's systems (activities, properties, collectibles) are open, so it is a good moment to start banking progress on the Stage 3 and 4 trophies between missions.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4. Unmissable, like the rest of the chapter set. Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, so once this pops, stop and clear any unfinished stranger strands and character finals (Stage 2) before you play the final mission — those are the trophies this guide flags as missable.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy: complete the game's final mission. The mission itself cannot be missed, but it is the point of no return this roadmap is built around — finish the stranger strands and the character-final trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) first, because strands tied to a character can close when the story ends. After the credits, the open world stays available for cleanup.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It is part of the main mission chain, so it unlocks on the way through the story with no side conditions. If a mission ever fails, retry from the checkpoint — story trophies only need the mission finished, not a clean run.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. A main-chain mission trophy: play the story and it comes to you. Heist missions tend to be the longer set pieces, so keep your vehicle repaired and your armor topped up before starting one — failing only costs a retry, not the trophy.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Another unmissable main-chain trophy. Nothing in the official description adds a side condition, so finishing the mission by any route the game allows is enough.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Main-chain and unmissable. Play the story missions as they unlock and this arrives with the rest of the Stage 1 set.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. Unmissable as part of the main chain. While VCIA is in play during this stretch of the story, also look at Catch Me If You Can (an unscheduled departure at VCIA) — this guide flags that one as missable because it is tied to VCIA access, so grabbing it around these missions is the safe play.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Main-chain, unmissable, no side conditions in the official description. Finish the mission and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own tracker — the gold capstone of the list. In practice this means finishing the story, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectible sets the completion percentage counts, so it overlaps heavily with the rest of this guide: a player chasing every trophy will be most of the way there. Check the in-game completion screen to see which categories are still short, clear them region by region, and leave this for last — when it pops, the platinum (Vice Got a Price!) follows if everything else is done.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — the official list tracks the count at 250. Stunts are the game's marked jump and trick spots, so the efficient route is to sweep them region by region as you explore, rather than hunting the last few at the end. Keep a fast vehicle for the longer jumps, and let the in-game map markers lead you: clear one area's stunts before moving to the next so the count climbs steadily toward 250.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type at least once — the official list counts 9 types. You do not need to win or finish with a good score; a single attempt at each type registers. The fastest way is to open the activities list in game, work down it one type at a time, and tick each off here as you go. Doing this early also introduces the activities that other trophies (races, fishing, the shooting range) build on.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 in total on the official list. This is one of the grindier silvers: gold usually means beating a target score, so expect to replay the tougher challenges. Work through the range's challenge list in order, learn each target pattern, and retry the ones you silver until they turn gold. The range stays open after the story, so there is no missable risk; just pace it across several sessions.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — the official list counts 14 locations. One win per location is enough; you do not need a perfect time. Tour the locations region by region, win each race once, and mark it off. If a course gives you trouble, a clean line usually beats raw speed in drone races — ease off on the tight turns and take the win on consistency.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the key word: the same race won twenty times does not count. Pick a spread of race types and locations, win each once, and keep a note of which ones you have banked. A tuned vehicle in the right class makes most races comfortable; if one race keeps beating you, move on and come back with a better car rather than grinding it.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the named opponent for the fishing activity, so find the fishing challenge, take Cal on, and out-fish him — the trophy needs the win, not just taking part. Fishing challenges are usually scored on what you land in the time given, so keep casting rather than waiting for the perfect spot, and retry freely: nothing here is missable.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game from start to finish. The shortest arcade cabinet you can find is the fastest route — the trophy only asks for a completion, not a high score. Play one game through to its end screen and it unlocks.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. This guide flags it missable: strands tied to one character can close when the story moves past them, and the official description gives no promise that Andy stays available after the finale. Safe play: as soon as Andy's strand opens, work it through to its final mission before you play the game's final mission. Finishing strands like this one also feeds Strangers & Freaks (8 strands).
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Flagged missable for the same reason as the other character finals: a strand belongs to its character, and story progress can close it. Do Kenton's missions as they appear and finish the strand before the game's final mission. Each completed strand also counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Treat it as missable: finish Billy's strand before the final story mission, while the character is certainly available. Playing strands promptly also keeps Strangers & Freaks (8 completed strands) on track.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. A strand is a short chain of missions for one stranger; the trophy counts finished strands, not individual missions. The five named character finals in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands, so completing those puts you most of the way to 8. Because strands can close as the story advances, this guide flags the trophy missable: sweep strangers as you meet them and have all 8 done before the final mission.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Flagged missable: character strands can close with story progress, so finish Randy's chain before the game's final mission. It also counts as one of the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Same missable logic as the other character finals: do it while Tyrone is available, before the final story mission. Completing it also advances Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — the official list counts 18 spots. This is a sweep trophy: travel region by region, use each spot once, and mark it off here so you never double back. Spots stay available after the story, so it pairs naturally with The Goodtime State (exploring all areas) — do both in the same tour of the map.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. This is tied to Bret's hunting requests: take his job, track the named animal, and bring it down. A unique animal means one specific target rather than any wildlife, so follow the hunt's own markers and instructions instead of free-roam hunting. If the animal escapes, re-accept or retry the hunt — the trophy only needs the successful hunt.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are scattered collectibles that belong to themed sets; finishing a set means finding every card in it. Track your sets in the in-game collection screen and hunt set by set — finishing three full sets is far more efficient than grabbing cards at random and hoping sets complete themselves. Nothing in the description ties cards to the story, so this is safe post-game cleanup.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the official list tracks the count at 100. WAiNK It spots are marked interaction points spread across Leonida, so treat this as a map sweep: work one region at a time and use the action at every marked spot. Because it overlaps with exploring (The Goodtime State) and the meditation spots, the fastest route is one combined tour where you clear every marker type in an area before moving on.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges from the game's challenge list. Challenges are the tracked mini-objectives (the kind of list the game keeps in its menus), and 50 completions is the target. Open the challenge list, pick the short ones first, and let the longer ones accumulate naturally while you chase other trophies — many challenges complete as a side effect of races, stunts and robberies. Check the list periodically so you can aim at the ones nearest completion.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner with you, reach a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely — the trophy needs the escape, not just the heat. Raise the wanted level together (robberies and mayhem with your partner present both count toward the setup), then break line of sight and stay out of the search cones until the stars clear. Doing it right after Retail Therapy works well: that trophy keeps the wanted level up through three shop robberies, and escaping afterwards can satisfy this one in the same run.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner alongside, without the wanted level ever dropping in between. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, rob the first, and drive straight to the next while the stars are still up — the level must never fully clear. If the heat fades between shops, stir it back up quickly (a fresh crime refreshes it) rather than starting over. Once the third robbery lands, escaping the 4-star heat can also earn Hot Together.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — the count is distinct vehicles, so hopping in and out of the same model does not advance it. The natural way is to drive something new whenever you see it: traffic variety, parked cars in different districts, boats and aircraft all add up over a playthrough. If you finish the story short of 100, tour the map's distinct areas (airfields, marinas, industrial zones) where the rarer vehicle types sit, and register finds in the Scooter Bros app as you go for On the Spot.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one use of Combat Focus, the game's slow-motion aiming ability. Set it up where enemies bunch together — a gang hideout or a robbery gone loud — then trigger Combat Focus with a full magazine and chain five takedowns before it ends. A weapon with a large magazine and fast handling gives you the most margin. If you fall short, let the ability recharge and try again on the next group.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — in plain terms, get out of VCIA in a way that is not the normal exit: steal an aircraft or vehicle and leave without clearance. This guide flags it missable because it depends on VCIA access, which the story controls (see the VCIA Takedown mission); the official description does not promise the airfield stays open for this afterwards. The safe window is while VCIA missions are active: once you are inside, take a vehicle or plane and go, and deal with the wanted level after you are out.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The official description is deliberately cryptic — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — pointing at the Rhino tank: get into a Rhino and make it hot, i.e. use the tank in combat and raise the heat with it. Steal or commandeer a Rhino where the military keeps them, then drive it into trouble until the wanted level climbs. Because the description gives no exact condition, treat the natural reading (cause mayhem in a Rhino) as the goal and keep going until it pops; heavy armor makes surviving the attempt the easy part.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at any point — no alarms raised on you, no witnesses spotting the robbery. Approach quietly, avoid cameras and staff sightlines, and take the goods without being seen; if you are spotted, abandon the attempt and try again rather than finishing loud, because a detected robbery does not count. Night-time attempts with fewer people around give you the cleanest run.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one — the escape matters: a vault robbery that ends in arrest or death does not bank progress. Vaults are the big-score robberies, so go in with armor, a fast getaway vehicle parked close, and a planned route out of the search area. Work through five separate vaults at your own pace; nothing ties them to the story clock, and the money feeds Treat Yo Self and the garage properties on the way.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks run set routes through the city — spot one, block or disable it, force the crew out or blow the rear doors, grab the cash, and lose the wanted level. The trophy needs the escape, so have a fast car ready and break line of sight quickly. One successful truck is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the official list counts 52 areas to discover. Flying or boating over an area usually registers it, so the quickest sweep is by air: cross the whole map in strips, then mop up any grey patches on foot or by road. Combine it with the meditation spots (18), WAiNK It locations (100) and vehicle discovery (100) so one grand tour advances four trophies at once. Check the map's discovered-areas progress to find the last stragglers.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — the official list counts 9 gangs, so you need one successful operation robbery per gang, not nine robberies of the same crew. Illegal operations are the gangs' money-making setups around the map; hit one for each gang and escape with the take. Keep a checklist of which gangs you have done (this tracker works) so you do not repeat a gang while missing another. The cash from nine operations also feeds the spending and laundering trophies.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach: find a beachfront spot on Ocean Beach that serves drinks, order a cocktail, and take in the view. It is one of the list's quiet moment trophies — no score, no timer. If it does not pop at the first spot, try another Ocean Beach venue with a sea view; the trigger is the combination of the drink and the location.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: get into a showroom car inside the dealership and drive it out through the glass frontage rather than using the door. The 'classic style' phrasing points at the showroom-window exit — take a car from the showroom floor and put it through the window onto the street. Expect a wanted level; escaping is not required by the description, just the smash-out itself.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — 'follow-through' is the bowling term the description plays on, so simply play a game of bowling at that named alley. The trophy is tied to that specific venue rather than bowling anywhere, so head to the Kolt & Associates alley, start a game, and bowl. It also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description is a pun — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — pointing at doing something notable together with your partner in front of a crowd: a public performance-style feat with mass appeal. The official list gives no exact condition, so the honest reading is: take your partner to a crowded public activity (the kind of venue with an audience) and complete it together. If it does not pop, work through the partner activities — the two named partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) show the pattern this one follows.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — PlayStation tracks this one with a count that runs to 500, so it is a long-tail trophy that fills up as you play: dialogue choices, mission decisions and everyday interactions all feed it. There is no single action to hunt; just play the game, engage with conversations and choices instead of skipping them, and let the counter climb. By the time you are deep into 100% completion it should be close or done — check your progress on the trophy card here.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — succeed at something on your second attempt after failing the first. The natural reading: fail an activity, challenge or mission objective once, retry it, and succeed. Deliberately failing a short challenge and immediately winning the retry is the controlled way to trigger it. Because the description names no specific activity, keep it in mind during Stage 3: the first time you retry anything and win, this may well pop on its own.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the description ('What the hell just happened?') points at one of the game's weird random events or easter-egg encounters. These are found by exploring rather than by following markers, so the honest advice is to roam Leonida's odd corners (the same tour that earns The Goodtime State) and stop for anything unusual you stumble on. Random events can be rare, so treat this as a by-product of the exploration stages rather than a target to force.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, swing a melee weapon at a person as you pass and connect. Ride as the passenger side or lean out while driving slowly past a pedestrian or biker, time the swing, and the knockdown should register. A quiet street with a lone pedestrian is the easiest setup; avoid crowds so the wanted level stays manageable.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and illegal operations; laundering turns them into clean money via your contacts, at a cut. The efficient loop is to rob (bank vaults for Maximum Withdrawal, gang operations for Pest Control, armored trucks) and launder the proceeds each time rather than hoarding marked bills. The $250,000 is cumulative earnings from laundering, so steady robbery income gets there well before 100% completion.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in shops, cumulative across every store. Weapons, vehicle upgrades, clothes and property-related purchases all add up over a playthrough, so this tends to complete naturally if you shop as you go. If you reach the endgame short, vehicle customization is the fastest sink: buy high-end upgrades and paint jobs until the total crosses $100,000. Laundered robbery money (Dime on the Dollar) makes the spending painless.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase every garage property — the official list counts 8. Garages are buyable properties dotted around Leonida; owning all eight also gives you storage and safe points across the map, which helps the exploration stages. Buy them as your money allows (robbery and laundering income covers them) and tick each off here. No story lockout is stated, so any you skip early can be bought in post-game cleanup.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. When you take a vehicle you like, register it in the app instead of just driving off — ten registrations is the target, and they can be any vehicles the app accepts. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles): while touring for new vehicle types, register the first ten finds and this trophy is done early.
trophies.name: On the Spot
